Your agents can now work through Google's Antigravity CLI.

## What's in 1.14.0

**Antigravity CLI as a harness.** Choose **Antigravity** on an agent's **Runtime** tab and the agent runs on Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`), with any model `agy models` lists, from Gemini to Claude and GPT-OSS. Conversations carry over from one run to the next and start fresh when the agent's workspace moves. Large agent instructions are no problem: the prompt goes to `agy` on stdin.

**Setting it up.** In the Terminal, run `kyoube harness install agy`, which runs Google's official installer into `/kyoubeai/.local/bin`. Then run `agy`, choose **Google OAuth**, open the link it prints, sign in and paste the code back. A Gemini API key works too: set `"modelProvider": "gemini"` in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the agent's environment. **Test** on the Runtime tab checks that `agy` runs and is signed in. The steps are in the [README](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/README.md#antigravity-cli).

**How it is wired.** Antigravity is not one of the core's own adapters, so KyoubeAI ships it in the image and registers it with the core at every start. Other external adapters you have installed are kept. If adapter management is hidden on your instance, registration is skipped with a log line, and plugin updates and the Kyoube skills carry on as before.

## Update

From 1.13, run `./update.sh`. It backs up first, and `./update.sh --rollback` returns to 1.13.0. Kyoube Studio moves to 0.6.1 on the first start. Afterwards the agent harness list offers **Antigravity**, and `kyoube harness list` shows `agy`.

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
